name: gmail.read_profile
description: Read the authorized Gmail account's own identity: the address it sends from, which is also what `me` matches in a search operator, along with its total message and thread counts. Use this instead of assuming which account is connected, and instead of inferring the account holder's own address from correspondence — a signature, a From header, or a name in a thread is somebody's claim about the account, not the account.

name: gmail.search
description: Search the authorized user's Gmail messages. Each hit returns its sender, recipients, subject, date, labels, snippet, and RFC Message-ID, so a search result is usually enough to answer who wrote what and when without opening the message.

query.description: Gmail search query. Supports Gmail's operators, for example from:dana@example.com, to:, cc:, subject:, newer_than:30d, older_than:1y, has:attachment, in:anywhere, is:unread, and OR / parentheses / "quoted phrases". Prefer an operator query over bare keywords, which match message bodies and return far too much.

maxResults.description: Maximum messages to return in one page. Defaults to 10.

pageToken.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier search, pass back the exact `nextPageToken` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor — a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `nextPageToken` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: gmail.find_contacts
description: Find a person's email address by searching the authorized user's prior Gmail correspondence for their name or partial address. Returns ranked candidate addresses with the evidence each was drawn from — how many messages it appeared in, when it was last seen, and the message it came from. Use this before addressing a draft to someone whose address is not already known; never guess an address from a display name or a company's domain. The authorized mailbox's own address is excluded.

name.description: The person's name, partial name, or partial address, for example "Dana" or "dana@".

maxResults.description: Maximum candidate addresses to return. Defaults to 10.

name: gmail.read_thread
description: Read every message in one Gmail thread, with bounded body text and attachment metadata. Takes the `threadId` of a search hit, not its `id` — the two are both bare hex and are not interchangeable.

threadId.description: The thread's id, copied from a search hit's `threadId` field, for example `18f0a2c4d5e6f701`. A search hit's `id` is the message's own id and names a different thread or none at all.

name: gmail.read_message
description: Read one Gmail message's body, headers, and attachment metadata. Takes the `id` of a search hit, not its `threadId`. Search results already carry sender, recipients, subject, date, and snippet, so call this only when the body itself is needed.

messageId.description: The message's id, copied from a search hit's `id` field, for example `18f0a2c4d5e6f702`. A search hit's `threadId` is the thread's id, not this.

name: gmail.create_draft
description: Create a Gmail draft for the authorized user and return its id and a link to open it. Drafts are not sent. Set message.kind to new and provide a subject, or to reply and provide an existing messageId; Rally resolves the reply's subject and threading. Create a draft when a person is expected to review the message first.

to.description: Primary recipients, as full email addresses copied from a tool result or supplied by the person. For a reply, explicitly choose who receives it; recipients are not added automatically.

cc.description: Copied recipients, as full email addresses. Omit or send null for none. They see each other and the primary recipients.

body.description: The message body, delivered as plain text exactly as written. Write plain text, not Markdown.

subject.description: The subject line for the new conversation, as plain text on one line.

oneOf.description: Allowed keys only: kind, to, cc, subject, body. Omit messageId and every threading field.

name: calendar.list_calendars
description: List the calendars this account can see, each with the id and name the other calendar tools accept. Call this to discover a calendar id, or pass a calendar's name directly to those tools and they will resolve it.

maxResults.description: Maximum calendars to return in one page. Defaults to 100.

pageToken.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier search, pass back the exact `nextPageToken` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor — a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `nextPageToken` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: calendar.list_events
description: List events in a time range, expanding recurring events into their individual occurrences and ordering them by start time. `timeMin` and `timeMax` are required and must be RFC 3339 timestamps that include an offset, for example 2026-08-11T00:00:00-07:00.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, "primary", or a calendar's name, which is resolved against this account's calendars. Defaults to the connection's configured calendar.

timeMin.description: Start of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-11T00:00:00-07:00. An event overlapping the window is included. A bare date such as 2026-08-11, or a timestamp with no offset, is refused; call the current-time tool rather than guessing the offset.

timeMax.description: End of the window, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-12T00:00:00-07:00. It is exclusive, so a whole day is that day's midnight through the next day's midnight.

query.description: Plain text matched against an event's title, description, location, and attendees. Omit it to get every event in the window. It is not a query language, so operators written into it are matched literally and return nothing rather than filtering.

maxResults.description: Maximum occurrences to return in one page. Defaults to 25.

pageToken.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier search, pass back the exact `nextPageToken` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor — a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `nextPageToken` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: calendar.read_event
description: Read one event, including its current attendee list. Read the event before changing its guests so a relative change is applied to who is actually on it.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, "primary", or a calendar's name, which is resolved against this account's calendars. Defaults to the connection's configured calendar.

eventId.description: The event's own id, as calendar.list_events returns it in each occurrence's `id`. It is not the calendar's id and not the title.

name: calendar.create_event
description: Create a calendar event. Listing anyone in `attendeeEmails` sends them a real invitation email, so treat this as an outward-facing write and source every address from a tool result rather than composing one. Start and end are RFC 3339 timestamps that include an offset.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, "primary", or a calendar's name, which is resolved against this account's calendars. Defaults to the connection's configured calendar.

summary.description: The event's title, as it appears in the calendar grid, for example "Design review".

description.description: The event's notes body, as plain text. Agendas, links, and context belong here rather than in the title.

location.description: Where it happens, as free text: a room name, a street address, or a meeting URL. It is a label, so this does not book a room or create a video call.

start.description: When it starts, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-11T09:00:00-07:00. Call the current-time tool rather than guessing the offset.

end.description: When it ends, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-11T10:00:00-07:00. It must be after the start.

timeZone.description: The IANA zone the event is anchored in, for example America/Los_Angeles. Defaults to the calendar's own zone. It decides what the event reads as after a daylight-saving change; it does not shift the offsets already written into start and end.

attendeeEmails.description: Guests to invite, as full email addresses, for example ["dana@example.com"]. Each one is emailed a real invitation, so take every address from a tool result rather than composing it. Defaults to none, which creates the event with no guests.

name: calendar.update_event
description: Update selected fields on an existing event. To change who is invited, say what changes — `addAttendeeEmails` and `removeAttendeeEmails` are applied to the event's current guest list — and use `replaceAllAttendeeEmails` only to set the entire list, dropping anyone left out. Any attendee change emails everyone who remains on the event.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, "primary", or a calendar's name, which is resolved against this account's calendars. Defaults to the connection's configured calendar.

summary.description: The event's title, as it appears in the calendar grid, for example "Design review".

description.description: The event's notes body, as plain text. Agendas, links, and context belong here rather than in the title.

location.description: Where it happens, as free text: a room name, a street address, or a meeting URL. It is a label, so this does not book a room or create a video call.

start.description: When it starts, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-11T09:00:00-07:00. Call the current-time tool rather than guessing the offset.

end.description: When it ends, as an RFC 3339 timestamp that includes an offset, for example 2026-08-11T10:00:00-07:00. It must be after the start.

timeZone.description: Re-anchor the event to this IANA zone, for example America/Los_Angeles. It cannot be sent on its own: a zone change is refused unless `start` and `end` are sent with it, so send all three. Omitting it leaves the event in the zone it already has.

eventId.description: The event's own id, not a calendar id.

addAttendeeEmails.description: Addresses to add to the event's current guest list. Everyone already invited stays.

removeAttendeeEmails.description: Addresses to remove from the event's current guest list.

replaceAllAttendeeEmails.description: The event's complete guest list after the update. Anyone omitted is removed. Cannot be combined with addAttendeeEmails or removeAttendeeEmails.

name: drive.search
description: Search accessible Google Drive files by name and by content. `query` is matched as plain text against both the file name and the indexed contents of Docs, Sheets, Slides, and PDFs — it is not a Drive query expression, so operators written into it are matched literally. Narrow with `fileType` and `modifiedAfter` rather than by describing the filter in `query`, and use `orderBy: "modified"` for the most recent rather than the most relevant.

query.description: Plain text matched against file names and file contents. Omit it to browse by fileType, modifiedAfter, and orderBy alone — for example the most recently modified spreadsheet.

fileType.description: Restrict results to one kind of file.

modifiedAfter.description: Only files modified after this RFC 3339 timestamp, for example 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z.

maxResults.description: Maximum files to return in one page. Defaults to 25.

pageToken.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier search, pass back the exact `nextPageToken` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor — a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `nextPageToken` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: drive.get_metadata
description: Read bounded metadata for one accessible Google Drive file.

fileId.description: The Drive file id, as drive.search returns it, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. It is the long segment in a Drive URL after /d/, not the file's name and not the whole URL.

name: drive.download
description: Read bounded text from a Drive file; binary content is never returned to the model.

fileId.description: The Drive file id, as drive.search returns it, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Use drive.export instead for a Google Doc, Sheet, or Slides file, which has no downloadable body of its own.

name: drive.export
description: Export a Google Workspace document to plain text or PDF.

fileId.description: The Drive file id of a Google Doc, Sheet, or Slides file, as drive.search returns it, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. An uploaded PDF or image is not a Workspace document; read one with drive.download.

mimeType.description: What to convert the document to. Use `text/plain`, which returns the document's text. `application/pdf` returns metadata only and no content — binary PDF data is never put in front of the model — so choose it only to confirm a PDF export is possible, never to read the document.

name: docs.read_document
description: Read the structure and bounded text of a Google Doc.

documentId.description: The Google Doc's id, as drive.search or docs.create_document returns it, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. It is the segment in the document URL between /d/ and /edit, not the title and not the whole URL.

name: docs.create_document
description: Create a Google Doc that subsequent Rally tools can edit, optionally with initial plain-text content.

title.description: The document's name in Drive, for example "Q3 launch plan". Drive allows duplicate names, so a title already in use creates a second document rather than opening the first.

text.description: Initial body content, inserted as plain text. Defaults to an empty document. Markdown is stored as its literal characters, so `# Heading` appears as those characters rather than as a heading.

name: docs.append_text
description: Append plain text to a Google Doc writable under Rally's per-file Google Drive grant.

documentId.description: The Google Doc's id, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Rally can only write to a document it created or that was shared with it individually.

tabId.description: Append into one named tab of a multi-tab document, as the `tabId` docs.read_document reports for that tab. Omit it for a document with a single tab, which is the usual case.

text.description: Plain text added at the end of the document, exactly as written. Start it with a newline to begin a new paragraph rather than continuing the last one.

name: docs.replace_text
description: Replace every exact occurrence of text in a Google Doc writable under Rally's per-file Google Drive grant.

documentId.description: The Google Doc's id, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Rally can only write to a document it created or that was shared with it individually.

find.description: The exact literal text to look for, for example "Q2 launch". It is not a pattern: wildcards and regular-expression syntax are matched as those characters. Text nothing matches changes nothing and is reported as zero replacements rather than as an error, so read the document first.

replace.description: What every occurrence becomes. An empty string deletes the matched text.

matchCase.description: Require the same capitalization as `find`. Defaults to true; set it false to match "launch" and "Launch" alike.

name: sheets.read_spreadsheet
description: Read bounded spreadsheet and sheet metadata from Google Sheets.

spreadsheetId.description: The spreadsheet's id, as drive.search or sheets.create_spreadsheet returns it, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Call this first to learn the exact sheet names the other Sheets tools need in a range.

name: sheets.read_values
description: Read bounded cell values from an A1 range in Google Sheets. Values default to what the sheet displays, so numbers arrive as locale-formatted strings such as "1,234.50" or "45%" and dates as text. Pass valueRenderOption UNFORMATTED_VALUE to get numbers and serial dates you can compute with.

range.description: An A1 range, for example `Sheet1!A1:D50`, or a whole sheet by name, for example `Sheet1`. Take the sheet name from sheets.read_spreadsheet and match it exactly; a range naming a sheet that does not exist is refused, while a correctly named range covering empty cells returns no values, which is a real answer rather than a failure.

majorDimension.description: Whether the returned array holds one entry per row or one per column. Defaults to ROWS.

valueRenderOption.description: FORMATTED_VALUE returns what the sheet displays; UNFORMATTED_VALUE returns computable numbers and serial dates. Defaults to FORMATTED_VALUE.

name: sheets.create_spreadsheet
description: Create a Google spreadsheet that subsequent Rally tools can edit, with optional named sheets.

title.description: The spreadsheet's name in Drive, for example "Q3 pipeline". Drive allows duplicate names, so a title already in use creates a second spreadsheet rather than opening the first.

sheetTitles.description: Names for the tabs to create, in order, for example ["Summary", "Raw data"]. Defaults to one tab named Sheet1. These are the names every later range has to use.

name: sheets.update_values
description: Replace cell values in a Google Sheet writable under Rally's per-file Google Drive grant.

spreadsheetId.description: The spreadsheet's id, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Rally can only write to a spreadsheet it created or that was shared with it individually.

range.description: The A1 range to overwrite, for example `Sheet1!A1:D50`. Writing starts at its top-left cell and covers as many cells as `values` supplies; a range larger than the data leaves the surplus cells untouched rather than clearing them.

values.description: The cells, as an array of rows in reading order, for example [["Name", "Owner"], ["Launch", "Dana"]]. Every row is one inner array even when there is a single column. Every cell in the range you send is written: `null` clears it exactly as an empty string does, so there is no per-cell way to say "leave this one alone" — to change part of a row, send a range covering only the cells that change. At most 10,000 cells in one call.

valueInputOption.description: How Sheets reads the strings you send. USER_ENTERED, the default, parses them the way typing would, so `=SUM(A1:A9)` becomes a formula and `10/6` becomes a date. RAW stores every string as literal text.

name: sheets.append_values
description: Append rows to a Google Sheet writable under Rally's per-file Google Drive grant.

spreadsheetId.description: The spreadsheet's id, for example `1A2b3C4d5E6f7G8h9I0j`. Rally can only write to a spreadsheet it created or that was shared with it individually.

range.description: An A1 range naming the existing table to add rows beneath, for example `Sheet1!A1:D1` or a whole sheet by name, for example `Sheet1`. Sheets finds the last populated row in that block and writes below it, so the range is a pointer at the table rather than the cells that change.

values.description: The cells, as an array of rows in reading order, for example [["Name", "Owner"], ["Launch", "Dana"]]. Every row is one inner array even when there is a single column. Every cell in the range you send is written: `null` clears it exactly as an empty string does, so there is no per-cell way to say "leave this one alone" — to change part of a row, send a range covering only the cells that change. At most 10,000 cells in one call.

valueInputOption.description: How Sheets reads the strings you send. USER_ENTERED, the default, parses them the way typing would, so `=SUM(A1:A9)` becomes a formula and `10/6` becomes a date. RAW stores every string as literal text.

insertDataOption.description: INSERT_ROWS, the default, inserts new rows and pushes existing content down. OVERWRITE writes into the rows already below the table, replacing anything there.
